findings.what: All seven puzzles put the right answer first, so after a couple of screens the button's position gives the answer away; vary the order as i1 does.
The Why? opens with "Still there.", a fragment that means nothing in a read-through; lead with the point instead, e.g. "A capacitor's reactance is 1 ÷ (2π × f × C)."

Screen 3 says each line charges and discharges its capacitors "60 times a second", but screen 2's hint says the plates do so every half cycle, which is 120 times a second; say "back and forth 60 times a second" or "60 cycles a second".
It never says why the body passes 190 mA, not the 287 mA of a solid fault on the same 1 µF; one sentence, "The body's 1,000 Ω holds it below a solid fault's 287 mA", closes the step.
"Two arrows 60° apart add to 1.73 times one of them" is stated bare; tie it to the 440 = 1.73 × 254 he already knows from star voltages, which uses the same geometry.

It tells him to "Drag the cable from 4 km to 8 km", but the opening demo has already moved the slider to 8 km by the time he reads it; say "Watch the cable go from 4 km to 8 km" or ask him to drag it back and out again.

findings.where: Screens 5 and 9, Current to earth readout (films s4, s8)
findings.what: The readout jumps to 287 mA or 190 mA in the first frame, while the arrows still show the healthy, cancelling set; let it follow the motion as the length readouts do on screen 7.

findings.where: Phasor panel, 60° label (moved state, 360 light and dark)
findings.what: The 60° sits at the obtuse 120° corner of the triangle with only a short dashed extension of L2, so it can read as the corner's own angle; lengthen the extension so the 60° plainly measures from L2's line continued to L3.

findings.where: Caption under the picture, screen 12 (360 end, 1280 end)
findings.what: The caption still reads "Example values: 440 V at 60 Hz, with 0.25 µF per km..." while the picture and question are the 480 V, 800 Ω case.

"Healthy charging, a line 96 mA" shows before charging current is introduced on screen 3, and on screen 2 the 1 µF and 96 mA tiles let him back out 254 ÷ 0.096 ≈ 2,650 Ω, the answer; hide the readouts until screen 3.

findings.where: Screen 3 moved state, phasor panel (360 light)
findings.what: In fault mode the panel leaves about 100 px empty under the triangle, which pushes the controls further down a phone screen.
It says the sum, "three times one line's", appears when "a fault or a person" gives it a way through, but through a 1,000 Ω person it is less (190 mA, not 287 mA, at 1 µF); say "up to three times".

Each repeats the show screen just before it almost word for word (double the cable gives 575 mA; a person on L1 carries current), so it tests the last sentence rather than the idea; screen 8 could triple the cable or add the ten drives instead.
